rv.q: ...never quite fulfils its potential, offering reflections and textures without cohesion. It all seems to end up working against the play, rather than enhancing it.
This play at the Arcola Theatre by Turkish director Serdar Biliş has a contemporary and experimental approach to Greek tragedy that doesn'

He uses a few tricks, some successfully, others less so, but the adapter/director is not hogging the limelight here (as too many do too often). The play still speaks with the power of its heritage and you just can’t avoid thinking about how many generations have been faced with its central dilemma and responded in the same way to the same pressures.

cn.t: Critics find this experimental take on Greek tragedy falls short of its potential, with contemporary elements failing to cohere into a satisfying whole.
